newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Clal Industries managing director resigns.
newsitem.headline: Clal Industries managing director resigns.

text.p: Yossie Rosen said on Thursday he was resigning as managing director of Clal Industries, the industrial-holding arm of Clal Israel, after less than four months on the job.

In a letter to Clal Israel chairman Leon Recanati, Rosen attributed his resignation to the board's decision to transform Clal Industries from a holding company into an investment company without management control of its group companies.
"This plan...doesn't enable me to utilise my managerial experience and does not provide the managerial challenge that I had expected when I accepted the position," Rosen wrote.
Rosen took over the position on a trial basis January 1 while staying on as managing director of Mashav Initiating and Development, a joint venture of Clal Israel and Koor Industries.
He said another reason for leaving was to devote his full attention to Mashav.

Clal Industries, hit by losses and writedowns at various group companies, reported a 14.6 million shekel ($4.3 million) loss in fourth quarter 1996, helping to reduce full-year 1996 net profit to 78.7 million shekels from 246.3 million shekels the year before.
Among its more troubled holdings are Scitex Corp, an electronics concern, and frozen-food maker Sunfrost Ltd.
A Clal spokesman said no replacement had yet been named.
